issues.span: they might bring me help and happiness
issues.evidence: Academic: all others bring benefit and happiness when amiably served; "might" weakens a plain statement, and "only" in the second half is not in the source.
issues.fix: If I serve and honor my other enemies kindly, they bring me help and happiness. But if I serve my troubling emotions, they bring me more suffering and harm.

issues.span: In battle, soldiers fight enemies who will die a natural death anyway. These soldiers ignore the suffering
issues.evidence: Academic: "If even those who desire to forcefully destroy [enemies made to suffer by natural death]... disregard the suffering... and do not turn back" - an if-even argument that 4-38 completes. The children's text states it as bare fact, losing the "if even" comparison.
issues.fix: If even soldiers fight enemies who will die anyway, and ignore the pain of arrows and spears, and do not run away before they reach their goal,

issues.span: it will certainly not make me despair
issues.evidence: Academic: "Needless to say, will not make me despair" - the a fortiori ("how much more me") completing the soldiers' example is reduced to a plain claim.
issues.fix: So of course I, fighting the enemy that causes all suffering, will not lose heart, even if it brings me hundreds of sufferings.

issues.evidence: Locked rendering for འགྲོ་བ is "being"; "wandering beings" adds a word and is inconsistent with "beings" elsewhere.
issues.fix: I am working for the happiness of all beings.
I promised to free the beings who fill space in the ten directions.

issues.evidence: Academic: "Therefore, in destroying afflictions, I shall never turn back" - a conclusion drawn from the madman remark, not a concession.
issues.fix: So I will never turn back from destroying my troubling emotions.

issues.evidence: Academic: "I shall be attached to this" - the referent is left unstated; "goal" is an added gloss.
issues.fix: I will hold tightly to this.

issues.span: Where did those groups of women come from?
issues.evidence: Tibetan མེ་ཚོགས is "masses/groups of fire"; the academic rendering "groups of women" appears to be a slip that the children's text copies. Ending the verse with women makes no sense after burning iron ground. Flag for human review of the academic line.
issues.fix: Where did those masses of fire come from?

issues.evidence: Academic: "the mind of renunciation" (locked: mind of giving up); the object "harmful actions" is not stated.
issues.fix: The perfection of good conduct is explained as coming from getting the mind of giving up.
